deliveryBrief: A woman aged105. Ancient, dry, papery voice with age-cracked creak, light breathy quaver and frail breath support. Soft low-mid register. Unhurried short phrases with small natural pauses. Warm, wry rural English manner; perfectly lucid and self-possessed. Clearly very elderly, not a young actress speaking slowly, not the firm resonant guard captain. No cartoon witch or theatrical croak. Speak only the dialogue.

audition.text: Sit down, dearie. I've waited a hundred years, I can wait while you sit.

lines.text: Sit down, dearie. I've waited a hundred years, I can wait while you sit.
Warm hands and empty heads. Ask yourself why, dearie.
The river remembers. Ask it nicely and it might tell you.
You've the right sort of face for questions. Ask me a better one.
Oh, never get old, dearie. It's dreadful. Wouldn't miss it, mind.
Mind the bank. It's softer than it was. Everything's softer than it was.
Never touched a shard. Not once. That's why there's still all of me.
Took you long enough. A hundred years I've sat here, and finally somebody comes knocking with a sensible face.
Go on, then. Ask me. Everybody asks the wrong thing, so I'll forgive you the first one.
Ah, there's my quiet neighbour. Never warmed your hands at the wrong fire, did you? That's why you can still think.
I told you a name once. You wrote it down, I watched you. Kept it safe, have you?
Corvin! Still counting his missing years, is he? Good boy. Reads by the wrong lamp, but a good boy.
Did you now. She and I are the last two in this valley who remember what we were told. Mind you keep her breathing.
Oh, dearie. She was the other one. The other one who still remembered. Now there's only me, and I'm tired.
Seven years old, I was, and up past my bedtime. The sky went red over the Keep, and the stars came down.
It didn't fall, dearie. It was thrown.
Falling things tumble. This came down straight, like a stone from a hand. Hissed in the river all night long.
And I'll tell you something else, since you've a sensible face. I saw who was standing on the hill when it came down.
That one. Same hood. Same face under it. A hundred years, and not one day older. I was seven, dearie, not blind.
If I knew that, dearie, I'd not have spent a century watching the water. Ask them. They'll answer you sideways.
I never once warmed my hands at that fire in the river. Think on why I'm the one who remembers.
Go on. Come back when you've better questions. I'll still be here. It's the one thing I'm good at.
The boy is by my fire. Let his father know. As for that old bear… hunger wakes before a creature does. Go gently, if you can.
Poor old thing. A hundred winters, and the last was the coldest. No, dearie. Keep the claw. There is nothing else down there to carry home.
